ei.title: Hyperreality and the Simulation of Reality
ei.subject: 수능특강

fullPassage: Jean Baudrillard, one of the best-known French social theorists, believes that the world of culture today is based on simulation, not reality. According to Baudrillard, social life is much more a spectacle that simulates reality than reality itself. People often gain "reality" from the media, where reality is not always as it might appear. Many U.S. children, upon entering school for the first time, have already watched more hours of television than the total number of hours of classroom instruction they will encounter in their entire school careers. Add to this the number of hours that some will have spent playing computer games or surfing the Internet. Baudrillard refers to this social creation as hyperreality — a situation where the simulation of reality is more real than the thing itself. For Baudrillard, everyday life has been captured by the signs and symbols generated to represent it, and we ultimately relate to simulations and models as if they were reality.

questions.passage: Jean Baudrillard, one of the best-known French social theorists, believes that the world of culture today is based on [simulation / imitation], not reality. According to Baudrillard, social life is much more a [spectacle / reality] that simulates reality than reality itself. People often gain "reality" from the media, where reality is not always as it might appear. Many U.S. children, upon entering school for the first time, have already watched more hours of television than the total number of hours of classroom instruction they will encounter in their entire school careers. Add to this the number of hours that some will have spent playing computer games or surfing the Internet. Baudrillard refers to this social creation as hyperreality — a situation where the simulation of reality is more real than the thing itself. For Baudrillard, everyday life has been captured by the signs and symbols generated to [represent / distort] it, and we ultimately relate to simulations and models as if they were reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) simulation=모의/시뮬레이션, (B) spectacle=장관/구경거리, (C) represent=나타내다/대표하다
det.analysis:
✅ ① simulation — spectacle — represent: 원문 일치. 오늘날 문화 세계가 시뮬레이션(simulation)에 기반하고, 사회 생활이 구경거리(spectacle)이며, 기호가 현실을 나타내도록(represent) 생성된다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ② imitation — spectacle — represent: (A) imitation(모방)은 simulation(시뮬레이션)과 유사하나 원문 단어가 아님
❌ ③ simulation — reality — represent: (B) reality(현실)는 spectacle(구경거리)의 대조 개념으로 부적절
❌ ④ simulation — spectacle — distort: (C) distort(왜곡하다)는 represent(나타내다)의 반의어 방향으로 부적절
det.tip: based on simulation(시뮬레이션에 기반) / a spectacle that simulates(현실을 모의하는 구경거리) / generated to represent it(그것을 나타내기 위해 생성된)

questions.passage: Jean Baudrillard, one of the best-known French social theorists, believes that the world of culture today is based on simulation, not reality. According to Baudrillard, social life is much more a spectacle that simulates reality than reality itself. People often gain "reality" from the media, where reality is not always as it might appear. Many U.S. children, upon entering school for the first time, have already watched more hours of television than the total number of hours of classroom instruction they will [encounter / avoid] in their entire school careers. Add to this the number of hours that some will have spent playing computer games or surfing the Internet. Baudrillard refers to this social [creation / destruction] as hyperreality — a situation where the simulation of reality is more real than the thing itself. For Baudrillard, everyday life has been [captured / liberated] by the signs and symbols generated to represent it, and we ultimately relate to simulations and models as if they were reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) encounter=마주치다, (B) creation=창조물, (C) captured=포착되다/사로잡히다
det.analysis:
❌ ① encounter — destruction — captured: (B) destruction(파괴)은 creation(창조물)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ② avoid — creation — captured: (A) avoid(피하다)는 encounter(마주치다)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ encounter — creation — liberated: (C) liberated(해방되다)는 captured(포착되다)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ④ encounter — creation — captured: 원문 일치. 수업 시간을 마주치고(encounter), 초현실이라는 사회적 창조물(creation)이며, 일상이 기호에 포착된다(captured)는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: instruction they will encounter(마주칠 수업 시간) / this social creation(이 사회적 창조물) / everyday life has been captured(일상이 포착되었다)

questions.passage: Jean Baudrillard, one of the best-known French social [theorists / practitioners], believes that the world of culture today is based on simulation, not reality. According to Baudrillard, social life is much more a spectacle that simulates reality than reality itself. People often gain "reality" from the media, where reality is not always as it might appear. Many U.S. children, upon entering school for the first time, have already watched more hours of television than the total number of hours of classroom instruction they will encounter in their entire school careers. Add to this the number of hours that some will have spent playing computer games or surfing the Internet. Baudrillard refers to this social creation as hyperreality — a situation where the simulation of reality is more real than the thing itself. For Baudrillard, everyday life has been captured by the signs and symbols [generated / eliminated] to represent it, and we [ultimately / initially] relate to simulations and models as if they were reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 (A), (B), (C)에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것끼리 짝지은 것은?

det.korean: (A) theorists=이론가, (B) generated=생성된, (C) ultimately=궁극적으로
det.analysis:
❌ ① practitioners — generated — ultimately: (A) practitioners(실천가)는 theorists(이론가)와 다른 의미
❌ ② theorists — eliminated — ultimately: (B) eliminated(제거된)는 generated(생성된)의 반의어로 부적절
❌ ③ theorists — generated — initially: (C) initially(처음에)는 ultimately(궁극적으로)의 반의어로 부적절
✅ ④ theorists — generated — ultimately: 원문 일치. 프랑스 사회이론가(theorists)이고, 기호가 생성되며(generated), 궁극적으로(ultimately) 시뮬레이션에 관계한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
det.tip: French social theorists(프랑스 사회이론가) / signs and symbols generated(생성된 기호와 상징) / we ultimately relate(궁극적으로 관계한다)

questions.passage: Jean Baudrillard, one of the best-known French social theorists, ①<u>believes</u> that the world of culture today is based on simulation, not reality. According to Baudrillard, social life is much more a spectacle that ②<u>simulates</u> reality than reality itself. People often ③<u>lose</u> "reality" from the media, where reality is not always as it might appear. Many U.S. children, upon entering school for the first time, have already watched more hours of television than the total number of hours of classroom instruction they will encounter in their entire school careers. Add to this the number of hours that some will have spent playing computer games or surfing the Internet. Baudrillard refers to this social creation as hyperreality — a situation where the simulation of reality is more real than the thing itself. For Baudrillard, everyday life has been ④<u>captured</u> by the signs and symbols generated to represent it, and we ultimately relate to simulations and models as if they were reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 사람들은 미디어로부터 현실을 '얻는다'는 맥락. lose(잃다)는 gain(얻다)의 반의어로 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① believes — 원문 일치. 보드리야르가 문화 세계가 시뮬레이션에 기반한다고 '믿는다'는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② simulates — 원문 일치. 사회 생활이 현실을 '모의한다'는 맥락에 적절
✅ ③ lose — 원문은 gain(얻다). lose(잃다)로 바꾸면 '미디어에서 현실을 잃는다'가 되어 본문의 '미디어로부터 현실을 얻는다'는 맥락과 모순 ←정답
❌ ④ captured — 원문 일치. 일상이 기호와 상징에 의해 '포착되었다'는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: People often gain "reality" from the media — 사람들은 미디어에서 '현실'을 얻는다(gain)

questions.passage: Jean Baudrillard, one of the best-known French social theorists, believes that the world of culture today is based on simulation, not reality. According to Baudrillard, social life is much more a spectacle that simulates reality than reality itself. People often gain "reality" from the media, where reality is not always as it might appear. Many U.S. children, upon ①<u>entering</u> school for the first time, have already ②<u>ignored</u> more hours of television than the total number of hours of classroom instruction they will encounter in their entire school careers. Add to this the number of hours that some will have spent playing computer games or surfing the Internet. Baudrillard ③<u>refers</u> to this social creation as hyperreality — a situation where the simulation of reality is more real than the thing itself. For Baudrillard, everyday life has been captured by the signs and ④<u>symbols</u> generated to represent it, and we ultimately relate to simulations and models as if they were reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 아이들이 TV를 더 많은 시간 '시청했다'는 맥락. ignored(무시했다)는 watched(시청했다)의 반의어로 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① entering — 원문 일치. 학교에 처음 '입학할 때'라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ② ignored — 원문은 watched(시청했다). ignored(무시했다)로 바꾸면 '수업 시간보다 더 많은 시간 TV를 무시했다'가 되어 본문의 TV 시청 맥락과 모순 ←정답
❌ ③ refers — 원문 일치. 보드리야르가 이것을 초현실이라 '칭한다'는 맥락에 적절
❌ ④ symbols — 원문 일치. 기호와 '상징'에 의해 포착되었다는 맥락에 적절
det.tip: have already watched more hours of television — 이미 더 많은 시간 TV를 시청했다(watched)

questions.passage: Jean Baudrillard, one of the best-known French social theorists, believes that the world of culture today is based on simulation, not reality. According to Baudrillard, social life is much more a spectacle that simulates reality than reality itself. People often gain "reality" from the media, where reality is not always as it might ①<u>appear</u>. Many U.S. children, upon entering school for the first time, have already watched more hours of television than the total number of hours of classroom ②<u>instruction</u> they will encounter in their entire school careers. Add to this the number of hours that some will have ③<u>spent</u> playing computer games or surfing the Internet. Baudrillard refers to this social creation as hyperreality — a situation where the simulation of reality is more real than the thing itself. For Baudrillard, everyday life has been captured by the signs and symbols generated to represent it, and we ultimately ④<u>object</u> to simulations and models as if they were reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 우리가 궁극적으로 시뮬레이션에 '관계한다'는 맥락. object(반대하다)는 relate(관계하다)와 의미가 상반되어 부적절
det.analysis:
❌ ① appear — 원문 일치. '현실이 항상 보이는 것과 같지 않다'는 맥락에 적절
❌ ② instruction — 원문 일치. '수업 시간의 총합'이라는 맥락에 적절
❌ ③ spent — 원문 일치. '컴퓨터 게임에 쓴 시간'이라는 맥락에 적절
✅ ④ object — 원문은 relate(관계하다). object(반대하다)로 바꾸면 '시뮬레이션에 반대한다'가 되어 본문의 '시뮬레이션을 현실처럼 받아들인다'는 맥락과 모순 ←정답
det.tip: we ultimately relate to simulations — 궁극적으로 시뮬레이션에 관계한다(relate)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: spectacle=구경거리/볼거리 (사회 생활이 현실을 모의하는 구경거리에 더 가깝다)
det.analysis:
❌ ① reality: reality(현실)는 spectacle과 대조되는 개념. '현실 자체보다 현실인 구경거리'라는 문맥에서 빈칸에 들어갈 수 없음
❌ ② television: television(텔레비전)은 미디어 매체이지 사회 생활의 본질을 묘사하는 단어가 아님
✅ ③ spectacle: 원문 일치. '사회 생활이 현실을 모의하는 구경거리(spectacle)에 더 가깝다'는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ creation: creation(창조물)은 보드리야르가 초현실을 지칭하는 데 쓰이지 사회 생활의 비유가 아님
det.tip: social life is much more a spectacle that simulates reality — 사회 생활은 현실을 모의하는 구경거리(spectacle)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: encounter=마주치다 (학교 생활 전체에서 마주칠 수업 시간의 총합)
det.analysis:
❌ ① generate: generate(생성하다)는 수업 시간을 '마주치다'가 아닌 '만들어내다'로 맥락에 맞지 않음
❌ ② capture: capture(포착하다)는 수업 시간과의 관계가 아닌 기호와 일상의 관계에 쓰임
✅ ③ encounter: 원문 일치. '학교 생활 전체에서 마주칠(encounter) 수업 시간의 총합'이라는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ simulate: simulate(모의하다)는 현실을 흉내내는 맥락이지 수업 시간과의 만남이 아님
det.tip: the total number of hours of classroom instruction they will encounter — 마주칠(encounter) 수업 시간의 총합

det.korean: captured=포착되다/사로잡히다 (일상이 기호와 상징에 의해 포착되었다)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 spectacle와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: spectacle=장관/구경거리/볼거리 → display=전시/진열/보여줌
det.analysis:
✅ ① display: display(전시/보여줌)는 spectacle(구경거리)과 '보여지는 것'이라는 의미를 공유하는 동의어 ←정답
❌ ② substance: substance(실체/본질)는 spectacle(겉모습/구경거리)과 반대 의미 방향
❌ ③ obstacle: obstacle(장애물)은 spectacle과 의미축이 완전히 다름
❌ ④ principle: principle(원칙)은 spectacle과 의미축이 완전히 다름
det.tip: spectacle = display = 구경거리, 볼거리, 보여주는 것

det.korean: encounter=마주치다/겪다 → experience=경험하다/겪다
det.analysis:
❌ ① avoid: avoid(피하다)는 encounter(마주치다)의 반의어
✅ ② experience: experience(경험하다)는 encounter(마주치다/겪다)와 '직면하여 겪다'는 의미를 공유하는 동의어 ←정답
❌ ③ produce: produce(생산하다)는 만들어내는 것으로 마주침과 의미축이 다름
❌ ④ ignore: ignore(무시하다)는 마주침 후 반응이지 마주침 자체와 동의어가 아님
det.tip: encounter = experience = 마주치다, 겪다, 경험하다

questions.passage: Jean Baudrillard, one of the best-known French social theorists, believes that the world of culture today is based on simulation, not reality. According to Baudrillard, social life is much more a spectacle that simulates reality than reality itself. People often gain "reality" from the media, where reality is not always as it might appear. Many U.S. children, upon entering school for the first time, have already watched more hours of television than the total number of hours of classroom instruction they will encounter in their entire school careers. Add to this the number of hours that some will have spent playing computer games or surfing the Internet. Baudrillard refers to this social creation as hyperreality — a situation where the simulation of reality is more real than the thing itself. For Baudrillard, everyday life has been captured by the signs and symbols <u>generated</u> to represent it, and we ultimately relate to simulations and models as if they were reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 generated와 의미가 가장 가까운 것은?

det.korean: generated=생성된/만들어진 → produced=생산된/만들어진
det.analysis:
❌ ① destroyed: destroyed(파괴된)는 generated(생성된)의 반의어
❌ ② consumed: consumed(소비된)는 만들어진 것과 반대 과정
✅ ③ produced: produced(생산된)는 generated(생성된)와 '만들어진'이라는 의미를 공유하는 동의어 ←정답
❌ ④ captured: captured(포착된)는 생성과 의미축이 다름 (잡는 것 vs 만드는 것)
det.tip: generated = produced = 생성된, 만들어진

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 reality와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: reality=현실 → fiction=허구/꾸며낸 것
det.analysis:
✅ ① fiction: fiction(허구)은 reality(현실)의 반의어. 실제와 꾸며낸 것의 대조 ←정답
❌ ② evidence: evidence(증거)는 현실을 뒷받침하지만 반의어가 아님
❌ ③ culture: culture(문화)는 현실과 의미축이 다름 (사회적 영역)
❌ ④ media: media(미디어)는 현실 전달 수단이지 반의어가 아님
det.tip: reality(현실) ↔ fiction(허구) — 실재와 꾸며낸 것의 대조

questions.passage: Jean Baudrillard, one of the best-known French social theorists, believes that the world of culture today is based on simulation, not reality. Baudrillard refers to this social creation as hyperreality — a situation where the simulation of reality is more real than the thing itself. questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ultimately와 의미가 가장 반대인 것은?

det.korean: ultimately=궁극적으로/최종적으로 → initially=처음에/최초에
det.analysis:
✅ ① initially: initially(처음에)는 ultimately(궁극적으로/최종적으로)의 반의어. 시작과 끝의 대조 ←정답
❌ ② frequently: frequently(자주)는 빈도를 나타내어 ultimately의 시간적 종결과 의미축이 다름
❌ ③ gradually: gradually(서서히)는 과정의 속도를 나타내어 최종 도달과 의미축이 다름
❌ ④ entirely: entirely(전체적으로)는 범위를 나타내어 시간적 종결과 의미축이 다름
det.tip: ultimately(궁극적으로) ↔ initially(처음에) — 최종과 시작의 대조

questions.passage: The police officer asked the witness to <u>gain</u> access to the building through the back entrance to collect evidence from the crime scene. People often <u>gain</u> "reality" from the media, where reality is not always as it might appear. In this sense, what we accept as real may be shaped by external sources rather than direct experience.
questions.stem: 다음 (A), (B)에서 밑줄 친 gain의 의미로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: gain: (A) gain access = 접근권을 확보하다/접근하다 / (B) gain reality from media = 미디어로부터 현실을 받아들이다/흡수하다
det.analysis:
❌ ① (A) 얻다 — (B) 얻다: 두 문맥 모두 단순히 '얻다'로 번역하면 의미 차이가 드러나지 않음
✅ ② (A) 접근하다 — (B) 받아들이다/흡수하다: (A)는 건물에 접근권을 확보하는 물리적 접근, (B)는 미디어로부터 현실 인식을 수동적으로 받아들이는 인지적 흡수 ←정답
❌ ③ (A) 확보하다 — (B) 이익을 보다: (B)는 이익이 아닌 현실 인식의 수용
❌ ④ (A) 도달하다 — (B) 증가시키다: (A)는 단순 도달이 아닌 접근권 확보, (B)는 양적 증가가 아닌 질적 수용
det.tip: gain: ① (물리적) 접근하다/확보하다 ② (인지적) 받아들이다/흡수하다

questions.stem: 다음 영영 정의에 해당하는 단어로 가장 적절한 것은? "the state of things as they actually exist, as opposed to an idealistic or notional idea of them"

det.korean: reality=현실 (이상적이거나 관념적인 생각과 대비되는, 사물이 실제로 존재하는 상태)
det.analysis:
❌ ① simulation: simulation(시뮬레이션)은 실제가 아닌 모의/가상
❌ ② spectacle: spectacle(구경거리)은 시각적 볼거리이지 실제 존재 상태가 아님
❌ ③ creation: creation(창조물)은 만들어낸 결과물이지 존재 상태가 아님
✅ ④ reality: reality(현실)는 '이상적/관념적 생각에 대비되는, 사물이 실제 존재하는 상태'라는 정의에 정확히 일치 ←정답
det.tip: reality = 현실, 실재. the state of things as they actually exist

questions.passage: According to Baudrillard, social life is much more a spectacle that __________ (simulate) reality than reality itself.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: 주격관계대명사 that의 선행사가 a spectacle(단수)이므로 3인칭 단수 현재형 simulates가 필요
det.analysis: a spectacle that __________ reality에서 관계대명사 that의 선행사가 a spectacle(단수)이므로 동사도 3인칭 단수형. simulate → simulates
det.tip: a spectacle that simulates reality — 현실을 모의하는 구경거리. 선행사가 단수이면 동사도 단수

questions.passage: For Baudrillard, everyday life has been captured by the signs and symbols __________ (generate) to represent it, and we ultimately relate to simulations and models as if they were reality.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 알맞은 형태로 바꿔 쓰시오. (영어로 쓰시오)

det.korean: signs and symbols 뒤에서 '생성된'이라는 수동 의미의 과거분사(p.p.)가 필요. generate → generated (과거분사로 명사 수식)
det.analysis: signs and symbols __________ to represent it에서 '현실을 나타내기 위해 생성된 기호'라는 수동 의미의 분사구문. generate → generated(과거분사, 수동)
det.tip: signs and symbols generated to represent it — 그것을 나타내기 위해 생성된 기호와 상징. 과거분사가 명사를 뒤에서 수식

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: hyperreality=초현실 (현실의 시뮬레이션이 실물보다 더 실재적인 상황을 보드리야르가 지칭하는 용어)
det.analysis:
❌ ① simulation: simulation(시뮬레이션)은 기법/과정을 뜻하지 보드리야르가 명명한 사회적 창조물의 고유 명칭이 아님
❌ ② spectacle: spectacle(구경거리)은 사회 생활의 비유이지 보드리야르의 명명 용어가 아님
✅ ③ hyperreality: 원문 일치. 보드리야르가 이 사회적 창조물을 '초현실(hyperreality)'이라 칭한다는 맥락에 부합 ←정답
❌ ④ instruction: instruction(수업)은 아이들의 학교 맥락 단어로 사회적 창조물 명칭과 무관
det.tip: Baudrillard refers to this social creation as hyperreality — 보드리야르는 이것을 초현실(hyperreality)이라 칭한다

questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: as if they were reality = 마치 그것들이 현실인 것처럼 (시뮬레이션과 모델에 현실처럼 관계한다)
